description: Tanzania Wami Ruvu Rufiji Flood Frequency Layer is a hazard data set listed in Africa GeoPortal (Esri), a continental ArcGIS Hub, published or maintained by Regional Centre for Mapping of Resource for Development. This product is one of the indicator layers selected in assessing vulnerability during Wami-Ruvu-Rufiji mapping. Flood frequency layer is an estimate of flood events in 100 years within the Wami Ruvu and Rufiji basins obtained from UNEP GRID.High flood frequency events translates to high exposure of a population or ecosystem, this has a linear relationship ... Coverage: Tanzania. The portal files it under the publisher Regional Centre for Mapping of Resource for Development. Its tags are wami, ruvuma, serviresa, rcmrd, wc-serviresa. The portal shows 2018-08-01 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is http://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/summary (as labelled on the portal). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support hazard exposure and risk screening for infrastructure. Related record: the catalogue-level record platform-africa-geoportal-esri.
